licenses.text:
Banjo Paterson, An Outback Marriage.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/banjo-paterson/an-outback-marriage

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Banjo Paterson, the author, died 1941.

First publication of the text used: 1906 (SE colophon: 'An Outback Marriage was published in 1906 by Banjo Paterson.'); the text was first published in 1900 as a serial in Melbourne (Wikipedia, An Outback Marriage)

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in Melbourne in 1900, not in the United States, so the US rule does not settle the origin. The edition's rights statement (quoted below) places the text in the US public domain.
- Country of origin (Australia): the text was first published as a newspaper serial in The Leader, Melbourne, from 13 January to 12 May 1900 (Wikipedia, An Outback Marriage: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_Outback_Marriage). The author died in 1941. Life plus 70 years ends on 31 December 2011, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 2012. A shorter term, if one applied, would have ended earlier.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'An Outback Marriage was published in 1906 by Banjo Paterson.'
- Wikidata Q436699 (Banjo Paterson), P570 = 1941-02-05.
- Wikipedia, An Outback Marriage (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_Outback_Marriage): originally published in The Leader, Melbourne, 13 January to 12 May 1900.
